reasoning: `WalletWallMultiSigVault` needs a recoverable verifier transition before a one-way verifier halt can safely apply to it.
The owner already exists, but delayed `pqVerifier` rotation is still a new authorization capability and must remain classified that way.
The rotation remains owner-only, subject to the existing 172,800-second delay and 14-day apply window.
The owner cannot move funds by virtue of the rotation alone.
The halt principal must never be able to rotate, become the consumer owner, or gain any verifier-selection/widening authority, including after ownership transfer.
A halted verifier identity may never be restored by deploying a fresh wrapper with the same verifier identity / `PROGRAM_VKEY`.
This acceptance does not waive TD1-N12, designation, code-hash, registry, per-chain execution, or successor-identity gates.
ownerDecision.operationalConsequence: WalletWallMultiSigVault joins the halt's scope through TD2-MULTISIG-ROTATION, as SP1-TD1 froze: the binding gate holds it to the same rules as the other consumers in scope (a haltable genuine wrapper, ACTIVE, not haltable by the signer, of no halted identity; off a local chain registered, the sole ACTIVE wrapper of its identity and designated) instead of refusing it every SP1-path verifier. It binds no production SP1 identity: no wrapper is registered on any chain, and the frozen implementation lane and real-value gates still stand.

stopCondition.text: if adding verifier rotation to WalletWallMultiSigVault creates an unacceptable authorization cut, STOP TD2-MULTISIG-ROTATION and return to design rather than weakening the one-way halt

td1N12.question: while a wrapper is halted no PQ-gated exit works, so the rotation delay gives no exit: is recovery-target gating (only a wrapper whose verifier code hash and PROGRAM_VKEY designation passed the SP1 evidence gates) enforced on chain or by process?
onChain: the delay (172,800 s) and the 14-day apply window, owner-only, a code-bearing target at proposal and at apply
the target is not HALTED, and a halted wrapper is refused as a first verifier

per consumer: the target's identity (SP1 verifier code hash, PROGRAM_VKEY) is neither the identity the current verifier was installed with, once it reports a halt, nor one the consumer recorded when it left a halted wrapper
the owner is never a halt principal of the current, pending or target verifier (constructor, ownership transfer, proposal, apply), by address
byProcess: the target's runtime code is the compiled ZKMLDSAVerifier (immutables masked, metadata excluded); it is ACTIVE, haltable and not haltable by the signer

its identity is not that of any halted wrapper in the WalletWall wrapper registry, read live, for every consumer; every reading fails closed: one the chain did not answer stops the gate, and a genuine wrapper that cannot be measured completely is refused
without the local override: it is registered and the only ACTIVE registered wrapper of its identity, so one halt call reaches every consumer
without the local override: its SP1 verifier's runtime code hash for the chain and its PROGRAM_VKEY match a designation, SP1-TD1's or a successor's

a consumer the halt's scope excludes is refused any SP1-path target (none since the owner admitted WalletWallMultiSigVault through TD2-MULTISIG-ROTATION on 2026-10-16; it is gated like the other consumers)
notYetEnforced: a successor designation for a recovery identity (the generated designation file and its CI subject check): until one exists the tooling admits no recovery from a halt of the designated identity off a local chain
registry entries that record the wrapper build they were deployed from, and a CI check that keeps the registry append-only, before the wrapper's compiled code changes (the review's R2-3)
td1N12.why: a consumer cannot recognise 'passed the evidence gates' on chain without a new authority to say so, and pinning a verifier code hash or a vkey in the consumer would refuse exactly the recovery targets (a fixed verifier has new code, a fixed guest a new vkey)

authorizationCut.whileHalted: holds no rotation and no ownership of any consumer (code)

no PQ-gated exit works (TD1-N12), so the delay protects no one; after it the owner can install any code-bearing verifier, letting anyone drain PqOnly vaults and reducing Hybrid vaults to ECDSA; target gating is process

no tenant can withdraw (TD1-N12), so the delay protects no one; after it the owner can install an accept-all verifier, voiding every tenant's p-of-q PQ signatures at once; each withdrawal still needs the tenant's m-of-n ECDSA signatures (executed); target gating is process

blockers: the owner's review and merge of TD2 (PR #216) as built and tested

the frozen implementation lane: the SP1 verifier code-hash pin in the wrapper, F-1, the designation file and CI subject check, the canonical-build workflow, deploy-zk-verifier's per-chain execution check, the runbook rewrite, proving availability
a real WalletWall proof (the real-proof lane)
